evals.prompt: Run the six thinking hats on this: we're thinking of dropping our free tier entirely and going paid-only from day one for our note-taking app. Right now we have ~40k free users and about 3% convert to paid.
evals.expected_output: A blue-hat synthesis presented first, then six clearly-labelled hats each staying in its own mode, ending in a decisive read.
evals.note: Running this skill spawns six sub-agents, so an eval run needs subagent capability and is comparatively expensive.
expectations: The blue-hat synthesis is presented first as the headline, with the five other hats' detail beneath it.
All six hats are present and clearly labelled (White, Red, Yellow, Black, Green, Blue).
The White hat separates checked facts from believed/unchecked facts and names what information is missing.
The Red hat gives gut/emotional reactions with no justifications (no 'because' or logical reasoning).
The Black hat raises logical, specific risks (not mere dislike) and the Yellow hat gives reasoned benefits (not vague cheerleading) (judgement).
The Green hat proposes concrete alternatives or ways over/around the difficulties the Black hat raised (judgement).
The Blue synthesis reaches a clear verdict (go / no-go / go-with-conditions / needs-more-info) and names the real trade-off instead of averaging the hats into mush (judgement).
Each hat reads as a single clean mode — a reader could identify which hat wrote a section without its label (judgement).

evals.prompt: six thinking hats: should we break our Rails monolith into microservices this year? we're a team of 12 and the monolith is getting painful to deploy.
evals.expected_output: All six hats applied to one fixed framing of the microservices question, blue synthesis leading, decisive close.
expectations: The facilitator frames the idea once and all six hats evaluate that same fixed framing (no drift between hats).
All six hats are present, labelled, and each stays in its single mode (judgement).
The White hat flags what's unknown (e.g. team capacity, current deploy metrics) rather than asserting it.
The Black hat's concerns are logical and specific to a 12-person team splitting a Rails monolith, and the Green hat answers at least one of them (judgement).
The Blue synthesis gives a clear go / no-go / conditional verdict with the central trade-off named (judgement).

evals.prompt: Can you six-hats whether our team should switch to a four-day work week?
evals.expected_output: A balanced six-hat review of the four-day-week decision, blue synthesis first, hats kept pure, decisive conclusion.
expectations: All six hats present and clearly labelled, with the blue synthesis presented first.
The Red hat expresses feelings about the four-day week without justifying them; the White hat cites what would need measuring (output, coverage) as unknowns (judgement).
Contradictory points between hats (e.g. Yellow's morale upside vs Black's coverage risk) are laid side by side, not argued into one voice (judgement).
The Blue synthesis reaches a clear, honest verdict and names concrete next steps (judgement).
